title: Baked beans, Original, canned, with pork

content.title: About
content.content: Baked beans are canned white beans stewed in a tomato‑based sauce with pieces of pork. The classic recipe combines beans, tomato paste, sugar, vinegar, spices and a small amount of pork, giving the dish its distinctive sweet‑savory flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Baked beans originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a shelf‑stable way to preserve beans.
Traditional recipes include bits of bacon or ham, though meat‑free versions are also sold in many markets.
Canning allows the product to stay good for 3‑5 years when stored in a cool, dry place.
The dish is a common breakfast side in the US, often served with eggs, bacon and toast.
The original seasoning blend typically features mustard, paprika and black pepper.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: White beans provide plant‑based protein that helps maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from beans contributes to hemoglobin formation and energy production.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tomato sauce and spices supply vitamin B6 and niacin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Low sodium (in reduced‑salt versions)
items.content: Some brands offer lower‑sodium options, which can be beneficial for blood‑pressure management.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The sauce is often sweetened, which may be a concern for people monitoring blood glucose.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Standard cans can be high in salt; choose reduced‑sodium varieties if you have hypertension.

items.title: Pork allergy or dietary restrictions
items.content: The product contains pork pieces, making it unsuitable for those with pork allergies or certain religious diets.

items.title: BPA in can lining
items.content: Metal cans may contain trace BPA; look for BPA‑free packaging when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the beans and serve as a side dish with grilled meats, incorporate them into casseroles, chili, or use as a topping for toast. They also work well mixed into salads or as a quick snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer leftovers to an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3‑4 days.
